title: Batch-aware stamped eviction proofs for KV cache correctness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Continuous batching and aggressive prefetching for low tail latency are causing subtle correctness issues in the GPU-resident KV cache. Under high concurrency we observed rare but repeatable cases where a prefix-prefetched entry was evicted while an in-flight batch still referenced it, leading to stale KV hits and occasional token generation divergence. Existing LRU/TTL heuristics do not capture batch liveness and prefix affinity simultaneously.
goal: Design and ship a practical eviction policy that composes LRU and TTL with a batch-aware 'stamp' and prefix quarantine semantics, plus a small set of provable invariants and automated tests that catch regressions. Implementation must be efficient on GPU slabs (low PTX/CUDA divergence), safe for continuous batching, and compatible with fallback strategies used by the smart router.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New stamped-eviction allocator integrated into KV runtime behind a feature flag.
2) Property-based tests (fuzz + linearizability harness) showing no stale-reference invariants violated under synthetic workloads that include prefetch/inflight batches.
3) Telemetry panels showing no increase in eviction-retry rate and a bounded increase in eviction latency percentiles.
4) Canary rollout with deterministic rollback if correctness alerts fire.
5) Documentation and design doc linked in ticket.
design_summary: We introduce a compact 'batch-stamp' per KV slot: (epoch, batch_seq). Every serving batch is assigned a monotonically increasing batch_seq within an epoch. Prefetch or insertion records the current batch-stamp. Eviction candidates are selected by combined score: age_score (LRU), ttl_score, and immutability_bonus if batch-stamp >= in_flight_min_stamp. Prefix-scoped quarantine: recently-prefetched prefixes enter a soft-quarantine window where only entries older than quarantine_window or safe-by-stamp are eligible for eviction. Key invariants: 1) Stamp monotonicity: stamps never decrease for a living entry. 2) No double-free: once an entry is freed, any batch referencing it must either have completed before free or its reference is atomically failed and retried by the caller. 3) Prefetch-safety: eviction cannot remove an entry with a stamp that is >= the global min in-flight stamp for any worker. Proof sketch and mapping to runtime fences included in design doc (see links).
implementation_notes:
- GPU slab allocator changes: store 32-bit stamp per slot packed with owner and refcount.
- Use atomic min/max operations available in CUDA for per-slotted stamp updates to avoid host roundtrips.
- Eviction probe runs on CPU fast-path but performs final atomic CAS on GPU-side slab metadata to claim a slot.
- Avoid heavy synchronization: maintain per-GPU local in-flight_min_stamp computed from batch tickets streamed from serving threads. Periodically aggregate to global only on epoch boundary.
- Fallback: when stamp-check fails due to race, eviction aborts and re-queues the slot for low-priority retry to avoid blocking latency-critical batches.
- Memory fragmentation mitigation: perform opportunistic compaction during low-util windows; prefer demotion (GPU->host) over raw free for large sequences to reduce slab churn.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: Stronger real-world guarantees under continuous batching and prefetch, low false-positive eviction of in-flight prefixes.
- Cons: Slightly higher metadata overhead (32 bits/slot) and modest increase in eviction decision CPU time. May increase minor p99 for eviction-heavy workloads if retry rates spike.
- Operationally: requires new telemetry and alerting; must be behind FF to limit blast radius.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for stamp monotonicity and stamp arithmetic.
2) Deterministic concurrency tests: simulate two workers racing to prefetch+evict the same prefix with controlled scheduling.
3) Fuzz harness adapted from eviction-sandbox to run millions of interleavings and check invariants (no double-free, no stale reads).
4) Integration canary against real workloads (chat and stream generation) with feature flag and shadow mode.
5) Stress job on dedicated ci-gpu fleet for 72h to surface fragmentation/latency regressions.
monitoring_and_alerts: Metrics to add: stamped_evictions_total, eviction_abort_retries, per_prefix_quarantine_count, in_flight_min_stamp_gauge, stamp_mismatch_errors. Alerts: eviction_abort_retries > 1000/hour OR stamp_mismatch_errors > 1/minute => rollback canary. Dashboards: eviction decision latency histogram by GPU and by prefix affinity.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Internal canary on staging traffic for 24h with shadow verification. 3) Small production canary (5% traffic) with rollback hook. 4) Ramp to 50% if no alerts after 48h, then full rollout. 5) Post-rollout retrospective and opt-in default removal of flag after 2 weeks.

notes: This ticket focuses on correctness guarantees rather than squeezing more throughput. A follow-up will look at an optimized low-overhead variant of the stamp for extremely latency-sensitive tenants.
